title: SPA/414/2021 of GARHWAL CO-OPERATIVE UNION THROUGH ITS GENERAL MANAGER Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
Page no. 1 of 3
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

SPA No. 414 of 2021
GARHWAL CO-OPERATIVE UNION THROUGH ITS GENERAL MANAGER
..................Appellant
Mr. Ghanshyam Joshi, Advocate

-versus-
 STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND OTHERS
.........Respondents
Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing Counsel for the State
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Mr. Rakesh Badola, Advocate for the respondent nos. 5 to 20
Sri S.K.Mishra, J.
Sri N.S. Dhanik, J.
 Date of hearing and Order: 29.11.2021
1. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
2. The appeal is filed against the final order passed by the
learned Single Judge, on 27.09.2021 in Writ Petition (S/S)
No. 902 of 2019. The petitioners-respondents no. 5 to 20
herein, in that writ petition prayed for the following
reliefs:-
"To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus to respondent no. 1 to 5 to pay the

Page no. 2 of 3
remaining dues of 13% of amount of calculated Ex-gratia under voluntary retirement scheme and the
arrears of salary of the petitioners and arrears of
revised pay under the recommendation of 6th pay
commission to the petitioners along with 18%
interest on voluntary retiral benefits, arrears of
salary and arrears of revised pay under the
recommendation of 6th pay commission from the
date of accrual.
3. The writ petition was allowed by the learned Single Judge
and in paragraph nos. 8 and 9 has observed as follows:-
"Learned counsel appearing for the respondent
no. 5 would submit that respondent no. 5 admits
the claim, but due to financial crises, the respondent
no. 5 is not in a position to make the payment. As
and when the financial condition of the respondent
no. 5 improves, the payment shall be made.
It is a petition, in which, the respondents have, in
fact, admitted the claim. Not only this, partially the
State had already made payment 13% of the ex-gratia amount under the VRS Scheme. In view of it,
the writ petition deserves to be allowed".
4. It is apparent from the record that respondent no. 5
admitted the claim of the petitioners who is in appeal
before us but it took stand that due to financial crises, the
respondent no. 5 is not in a position to make the
payment; such a plea is not tenable in the eyes of law.

Page no. 3 of 3
5. The financial crisis is not a ground to deny the legitimate
dues of employees in view of the admission of the claim
of the petitioner before the learned Single Judge. We are
inclined to dismiss the appeal. Ordered accordingly.
